column1: # Per-file real macOS bats wall time (seconds), used by shard-tests.sh to
# weight the CI partition by measured cost instead of @test count (#1243).
# @test count is a loose, occasionally blind proxy for a file's real cost:
# a file whose time is almost entirely waiting (background processes, poll
# loops) can carry a tiny count while dominating its shard's wall clock, and
# a file that is merely large in @test count is not necessarily slow. This
# table sidesteps the proxy by using each file's own measured time directly.
# MEASURED AGAINST: GitHub Actions run 35563098757 (main, tests.yml bats
# job, macos-latest, 5 shards, 2026-09-21). Every shard in that run
# completed (none timed out), so every file below has a real file_end
# record -- summed from the run's 5 bats-timings-macos-latest-* artifacts
# this run brought the heaviest of the current 5 shards from 1132s down to
# 839s (#1304 CI-capacity work: the shard split itself was fine, this table
# had just gone stale -- see that run's own per-file numbers for detail).
# The suite's total real time also fell in this window (old table sum
# 6249s over the files common to both tables vs 4173s now), and that fall
# is two real perf fixes, not broad drift: test_remote_engine_start_refusal.bats
# (shortened the two slowest tests' production-readiness wait). A third
# file, test_watch.bats, measured 317s->2s in this same run, but that 2s is
# NOT a speedup -- the file is quarantined as a whole for #1262 (setup()
# skips every test unconditionally, see below), so 2s is "did not run",
# not "got faster". Its row below is pinned to 317s, its last real
# pre-quarantine measurement, rather than the misleading 2s (see that row's
# own comment). Every other file moved by single-digit seconds either way.
# So this window's imbalance was not organic, even drift -- it was two real
# fixes plus one quarantine not being reflected in the table, and none of
# those is the kind of thing that keeps happening on a schedule; each only
# moves this table when something specific (a perf fix, a quarantine, an
# un-quarantine) actually happens to a file. Update-on-notice, prompted by
# exactly that kind of change, stays the right call -- no scheduled or
# A file with no row here (renamed, or added after this measurement) is
# estimated at this table's own average seconds/file by shard-tests.sh,
# never treated as zero-cost or dropped from the partition -- coverage does
# not depend on this table being current. tests/test_ci_sharding.bats's
# balance-ratio assertion checks the computed partition against THIS
# table's own numbers, not against a live run, so it cannot detect this
# table drifting out of sync with reality -- only a human noticing a real
# run's shard skew (as happened here) triggers a refresh. Refresh by
# re-running this extraction against a green run's bats-timings artifacts.
# Columns: basename<TAB>seconds. Sorted by basename for a legible diff.
# Pinned to 317s, the last real pre-quarantine measurement (run 34845597032,
# 2026-09-14), NOT this run's 2s -- the whole file is quarantined for #1262
# (setup() skips every test unconditionally, tracked by #1318), so 2s means
# "did not run", not "got faster". Update this back to a real measurement
# once #1318 un-quarantines the file; until then a refresh against a run
# where it's still quarantined must keep reusing 317, not overwrite it with
# whatever near-zero number that run measures.
